name: Question 1
problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a=⟨2t,1-2t⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨0,0⟩$ when $t=1$, calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨2t,1-2t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 2t\,\text{d}t,\int (1-2t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}+{C}_{1},t-{t}^{2}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(1)=⟨0,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨{1}^{2}+{C}_{1},1-{1}^{2}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,0⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{1},{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =1+{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{1} & =-1,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & ={C}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
v=⟨{t}^{2}-1,t-{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Question 1
?

The acceleration a at time t of a particle P moving in the xy-plane is given by a=⟨2t,1−2t⟩. Given that the particle has velocity v=⟨0,0⟩ when t=1, calculate the velocity vector of P at time t.

a
v=⟨t2,2+t−t2⟩
b
v=⟨3t2−1,2t−t2⟩
c
v=⟨2t2−1,2t−t2⟩
d
v=⟨t2−1,t−t2⟩
e
v=⟨t2−1,2+t−2t2⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector: v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫⟨2t,1−2t⟩dt=⟨∫2tdt,∫(1−2t)dt⟩=⟨t2+C1,t−t2+C2⟩

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that v(1)=⟨0,0⟩. Substituting t=1, we get v(1)=⟨12+C1,1−12+C2⟩⟨0,0⟩=⟨1+C1,C2⟩.

So, we must have 0=1+C1C1=−1,

and 0=C2.

Therefore, the velocity vector is v=⟨t2−1,t−t2⟩.
